title: Finite expressions of formal coefficient operators
statement: Let R be a commutative ring. For n,k,m,l nonnegative integers, finite coefficient expressions from k-tuples of R[[T_1,...,T_n]] to l-tuples of R[[V_1,...,V_m]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] are the inductively generated expressions with matching boundaries: identity, addition, composition, componentwise multiplication by specified full series, insertion along an injection of variable sets, partial coefficient extraction, and action by a finite l-by-k matrix over R [def-weil-matrix]. A partial coefficient test consists of an injection i:Fin a into Fin n and an exponent beta on Fin n vanishing on the image of i; its value on H has coefficient at gamma equal to the coefficient of H at beta+i_*gamma, thus retains all complementary coefficients as a full series. Evaluation performs the specified operations, with matrix action given by finite sums. A specified inverse matrix is represented by its given entries in the same matrix constructor. A coefficient ring homomorphism transports expressions recursively by mapping all stored scalar entries and all coefficients of stored series, leaving index data fixed. scalarEval is evaluation on the unique component of a one-component tuple. The coefficient topology on each tuple is the product topology with discrete scalar coefficients. The common kernel of any family of partial coefficient tests is the set of series for which every test vanishes as a full series. An expression is a projection onto that kernel if its image lies in the kernel and it fixes every member. Its ideal correction for a finite family f is the assertion that P(H)-H lies in the ideal generated by f for every unrestricted input H. Finally flattening R[[X]][[T]] to R[[X,T]], and its inverse, are the maps that regroup coefficient families using the bijection between exponents on a disjoint union and pairs of exponents. Zero variables, zero tuple sizes and empty families are permitted.

source.place: Tags 0306 (lemma-Noetherian-power-series) and 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, part (2): Krull intersection for an ideal in the Jacobson radical; 00IP is its local case) supply Noetherianity of S[[T]] and (T)-adic closedness of its ideals, (T) lying in the Jacobson radical of S[[T]]. The operator assertion is an agent lemma extending the coefficient transport in Bierstone--Milman 1997, Remark 9.11; no Stacks tag states the combined assertion.
